learning_outcomes.text: Be able to explain the basic concepts and historical development of Industrial Engineering.
Be able to use Industrial Engineering methodologies and techniques in various applications.
Be able to apply system approach and problem-solving techniques in different scenarios.
Understand production planning, inventory management, and control techniques, and be able to perform basic analyses in these areas.
Be able to explain and apply quality control, improvement methodologies, and process analyses.
Have knowledge of work study and ergonomics, and be able to develop process improvement suggestions considering human factors.
Be able to solve optimization and decision-making problems using operations research techniques.
Recognize emerging trends such as sustainability, Industry 4.0, and IoT in Industrial Engineering, and be able to evaluate their effects.
Be able to relate theoretical knowledge with case studies and real-world applications.

syllabus_topics: Sustainable production and emerging trends like Industry 4.0
assessment_rules: The overall success score is determined by the contribution of semester learning activities and the end-of-semester examination. The Midterm Examination contributes 100% to the Semester Learning Activities, and the Final Examination contributes 100% to the End of Semester Learning Activities. The Semester Learning Activities have a 40% weight, and the End of Semester Learning Activities have a 60% weight on the final grade.
